title.narrative: Urgent Early Recovery and Resilience building in Syria Cities

description.narrative: The project aims to enhance the resilience of crisis-affected vulnerable communities, especially returnees and female-headed families; and contribute to early recovery in the target cities through the rehabilitation of prioritized basic socio-economic infrastructure based on the area-based community-led neighborhood action plans. A resilience approach is required to complement lifesaving humanitarian activities to address the growing needs of people, as discussed in the Brussels VI Conference and a new UN Strategic Framework 2022-2024. The de-centralized area-based approach to supporting communities has been demonstrated to be effective and efficient in strengthening the resilience of affected people in the previous UN-Habitat projects supported by the Japanese government. In the backdrop of the continued deterioration of service, environment, and social challenges associated with cumulative impacts on people, the de-centralized and inclusive planning that engages with vulnerable communities has been contributing to enhancing and restoring the social cohesion in the targeted cities and neighborhoods. The project contributes to human security through its people-centred response. It will put a wide range of community members at the centre of the planning, designing and decision-making process and create a space for communities to work together. The project will also empower people by developing their capacities to engage in the planning and decision-making process, and at the same time protect them by improving the resilience of the community by restoring public services.
